content.study:
Article 390 (“Money received or raised or expenditure incurred between the commencement of the Constitution and the 31st day of March, 1950”) of the Constitution of India has been omitted by constitutional amendment.

Status: Repealed / Omitted.
It is not current working law in the territory of India.

Examination Instruction:
When answering university or judicial service questions, note that Article 390 is omitted and identify the living constitutional or statutory provision that currently governs the subject matter.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the constitutional status and historical context of Article 390 (Money received or raised or expenditure incurred between the commencement of the Constitution and the 31st day of March, 1950).
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
I. INTRODUCTION & STATUS
Article 390 of the Constitution of India (“Money received or raised or expenditure incurred between the commencement of the Constitution and the 31st day of March, 1950”) is omitted. It does not form part of the living, enforceable constitutional text.

II. HISTORICAL BACKGROUND
The provision was repealed/omitted by constitutional amendment to remove obsolete structures, harmonize constitutional governance, or eliminate transitional provisions.

III. CURRENT GOVERNING HEADING
Examinees must identify the living provision that now regulates this field (e.g. general powers of Parliament, corresponding statutory enactments, or alternative constitutional mechanisms).

IV. CONCLUSION
Cite Article 390 strictly as a repealed/omitted heading. Do not apply its text to contemporary 2026 dispute scenarios.
